subject: Dedicated capacity - post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Elena & Tom,

Thanks again for the time this morning — good discussion and appreciate the transparency on latency and compliance needs. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Bursty inference traffic during peak clinic hours causing tail latency spikes and occasional queueing
- Requirement for data isolation and strict access controls (PHI for some models)
- Need predictable per-token economics and a clear SLA for production traffic

Goals we heard:
- P95 latency under 250ms for primary text-generation endpoints
- Dedicated, customer-isolated GPU pool with KMS/HSM integration for keys
- Ability to autoscale for predictable weekday peaks without impacting baseline SLAs

High-level recommended approach (Dedicated):
- Pilot: 4 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs for 4 weeks to validate latency and integration
- Production: Baseline 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale to 12 for peak windows; burst fallback to shared capacity for rare events
- Runtime config: batching + KV cache to reduce per-token cost; model quantization recommendations after pilot
- SLA targets: 99.95% uptime, p95 latency goal <250ms (we’ll run a latency profile during pilot to verify)

What we’ll deliver next: 
- Marissa will follow up with a detailed dedicated capacity plan, estimated committed spend, and a draft quote (including pilot pricing).
- Ben will intro procurement contacts and share HubSpot deal link.
- Elena / Tom to confirm procurement point-of-contact and share SOC2/security questionnaire.

If that matches your understanding, Marissa will send the plan & quote later today or tomorrow. Proposed pilot kickoff window: week of May 25.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0183

Thanks Ben — this looks right at a high level. A few clarifying Qs from my side: 

1) Data encryption: we need confirmation that data-at-rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys (we use AWS KMS/HSM). Is Redwood able to support CMK/HSM integration for the dedicated deployment?
2) Key access controls and audit logs: we need an auditable trail showing which Redwood principals accessed keys; is that data surfaced in your audit logs?
3) Cost: can you provide a ballpark of committed monthly spend for the Production configuration you recommended? We need that for our budgeting conversation.

Attaching our security questionnaire; procurement will want answers inline. I’ll loop them in once we have the quote.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Elena / Tom — great to join the thread. I’m attaching a first-pass dedicated capacity plan and a draft quote for ACME-2345. High level answers to Elena’s questions below and details are in the attached plan.

Security & keys:
- We support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) for dedicated/private deployments; keys can be rotated and we can integrate with your HSM for higher assurance.
- Audit logs: we provide request-level audit logs that include key usage events and actor principals; logs can be exported to your logging endpoint or pushed to S3 with retention policy you specify.

Capacity & cost (high-level):
- Production recommendation: 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (baseline) with autoscale to 12 GPUs during weekday peak windows and controlled burst to shared capacity for rare spikes.
- Pilot: 4 reserved GPUs for 4 weeks (we’ll mirror production traffic patterns for validation).
- Estimated committed monthly spend (Production config): ~$35,000/month (includes reserved GPU compute + support + observability). Pilot pricing (4 GPUs): ~$12,000/month for the pilot period.

SLA and telemetry:
- Target SLA: 99.95% uptime for the dedicated pool.
- Latency SLO: expected p95 <250ms for the configured model and batch sizing; we will run a profiling run during the pilot and adjust batching/quantization to meet target.

Scaling plan:
- Autoscale policy: scale by queued requests and token throughput thresholds; pre-warmed workers to avoid cold-start tail latency.
- Cache strategy: prefix/KV cache for common prompts to reduce effective load.

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa: attach detailed plan + draft quote (attached). Will also generate a DocuSign ready quote if ACME approves the pilot.
- Ben: introduce procurement and schedule pilot kickoff for week of May 25.
- Elena / Tom: share procurement contact and provide sample traffic (peak QPS and representative prompt set) so we can finalize profiling.

Attachments: dedicated_capacity_plan_v1.pdf, redwood-dedicated-quote-acme-ACME-2345.pdf

Thanks — Marissa

--
